visa_routes.name: Critical Skills Employment Permit (CSEP)

salary_threshold.note: From 2026-03-01: €40,904 for Critical Skills Occupations List roles (incl. ICT professionals) with a relevant degree; €36,848 if qualification obtained within previous 12 months; over €68,911 for any occupation not on the Ineligible List where the applicant has no degree but the necessary experience. Previously €38,000 / €64,000. Job offer must be ≥2 years.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: Relevant degree or higher for the €40,904 tier; no degree needed at €68,911+ with relevant experience.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Unclear whether DETE treats a 3-year Indian bachelor's as a 'relevant degree' (no official statement found). For senior engineers paid €68,911+, the no-degree tier applies, so degree recognition is moot.
visa_routes.processing_time: As of 2026-11-20 DETE was processing CSEP applications received 2026-10-23 (~4 weeks). Apply ≥12 weeks before start date per DETE.
visa_routes.lottery_or_quota: No lottery or cap; no Labour Market Needs Test for CSEP.
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Stamp 4 (no permit needed) after 21 months of employment in the State on the CSEP (irishimmigration.ie); long-term residence after 60 months of permission.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: €1,000 permit fee (90% refunded if refused); employer or employee may pay (not verified who must). No sponsor licence; Trusted Partner status speeds employer applications.

visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Not researched; most software roles qualify for CSEP instead.
visa_routes.processing_time: As of 2026-11-20 DETE processing new GEP applications received 2026-10-23.
visa_routes.lottery_or_quota: No lottery; Labour Market Needs Test generally required (details not re-read).
visa_routes.path_to_pr: Stamp 4 after 57 months of employment (per practitioner summaries; not read on official page).
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: Permit fee not re-read for GEP.

sponsor_register.name: DETE 'Employment permits issued to companies' (annual statistics)
sponsor_register.update_frequency: Monthly refresh during the year; covers 1 January to the last day of the previous month (2026 file published 2026-11-09, covering to end Oct 2026). Yearly pages back to 2009.
sponsor_register.how_to_use: Download employment-permits-issued-to-companies-<year>.xlsx (current + previous year), normalise employer names (lowercase, strip Ltd/Limited/DAC/Teoranta/Unlimited Company/plc, punctuation) and fuzzy-match job companies; a company that received permits recently has hired non-EEA staff. It is not a licence register (Ireland has no sponsor licence) and does not break down by permit type per company.

negative: must have the right to work in Ireland

ease_for_indian_nationals.rationale: ICT professionals are on the Critical Skills list: no lottery, no labour market test, processing ~4 weeks, Stamp 4 (open work rights) after 21 months, and English is the working language. For senior pay above €68,911 no degree is needed, which avoids any 3-year-degree question. The downsides are a small market concentrated in Dublin, EU candidates often being preferred, and a housing shortage.

factors.degree_recognition: Relevant degree needed only for the €40,904 tier; unclear for 3-year degrees; not needed above €68,911.
factors.employer_willingness: Multinationals in Dublin routinely use CSEP; SMEs less so.
factors.attestation_or_paperwork: Employer applies online (EPOS); after arrival register with immigration (IRP).

scam_warnings: Agents charging fees for a 'guaranteed Critical Skills permit': the employer applies on DETE's EPOS system; check the employer on the DETE companies-issued-permits list and CRO.
